title: The Sikh Religion
transliteration: The Sikh Religion: Its Gurus, Sacred Writings and Authors
author: max-arthur-macauliffe
attributionNote: Max Arthur MacAuliffe (1842–1913), an Irish civil servant in the Punjab, wrote this six-volume account of the Sikh Gurus and their writings. Volume 1, the only volume the archive carries, is devoted to Guru Nanak: a long introduction on the Punjab and the religious setting, a life in seventeen chapters, and translations of the Japji, Asa ki War, the Rahiras, the Sohila and a selection of hymns and sloks.
description: The Sikh Religion is the first comprehensive English account of the Sikh tradition and its scriptures. Volume 1 sets the scene in the Punjab of Guru Nanak's time, follows his life through the traditional janamsakhi material, and then gives the reader the Guru's own words: the Japji, the evening and morning liturgies, Asa ki War, and a large body of hymns and additional sloks translated in full. MacAuliffe writes as a nineteenth-century historian, weighing the janamsakhis against one another; the book is valuable both for its narrative and for making the early Gurbani available in English before the modern translations.
historicalContext: MacAuliffe served in the Punjab administration and spent years with the texts and with Sikh scholars. Oxford University Press published the six volumes between 1909 and his death in 1913, with the last volumes seen through the press by his colleagues. Volume 1 remains a standard Victorian introduction to Guru Nanak; its translations are the ones later writers often quote, and its account of the sources is still cited in janamsakhi scholarship.
availabilityNote: Volume 1 only. The Internet Sacred Text Archive carries the introduction, the seventeen chapters on Guru Nanak's life, and the translations of the Japji, Asa ki War, Rahiras, Sohila, hymns and additional sloks — twenty-four chapters in all, streamed at read time. Volumes 2–6, which cover the later Gurus, are not on the archive and are recorded in the acquisition register.
